class_name Archer
extends Node2D
## The hero on the wall walk: slides along X only and fires on its own (GDD 5.1, 6.2).
## Aims at the nearest scarecrow inside the upward cone; holds fire when there is none.
## Owns the shot state machine (CHANGE-BRIEF §5, §6): it decides when to draw (travel("shoot")) and
## when to cancel (playback.start("idle")); the AnimationTree only plays the clips and keys
## release_window, which this script reads and never writes.

signal fired(arrow: Arrow)

const ARROW_SCENE := preload("res://game/arrow.tscn")
## s; the draw starts when fire_cooldown is at most this (brief §5.2: 18 ticks from travel("shoot")
## to the first true read of release_window, so back-to-back shots keep the 36-tick cadence).
## Here, not in tuning.gd, because tuning.gd is out of scope for this change.
const DRAW_LEAD := 0.3

var arrows_parent: Node
var fire_cooldown := 0.0
var release_window := false          # written only by Archer/AnimationTree (idle and shoot clips)
var shot_armed := false              # true from travel("shoot") until the arrow, a cancel or a restart
var locked_target: Scarecrow = null  # taken when the draw starts (brief §5.3)
var _locked_pos := Vector2.ZERO      # locked target's global position, recorded every armed tick

@onready var _playback: AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback = $AnimationTree.get("parameters/playback")


func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void:
	var axis := Input.get_axis("move_left", "move_right")
	position.x = clampf(position.x + axis * Tuning.ARCHER_SPEED * delta,
			Tuning.ARCHER_MARGIN, Tuning.VIEW.x - Tuning.ARCHER_MARGIN)
	fire_cooldown = maxf(fire_cooldown - delta, 0.0)
	if shot_armed:
		if release_window:
			# Active frame: the arrow goes even if the target was lost on this same tick (§5.5).
			var aim := locked_target.global_position if is_instance_valid(locked_target) else _locked_pos
			_fire_at(aim)
			fire_cooldown = Tuning.FIRE_INTERVAL
			shot_armed = false
			locked_target = null
		elif not _target_held():
			cancel_shot()   # startup: target died or left the cone; no new draw on this tick
		else:
			_locked_pos = locked_target.global_position
		return
	if fire_cooldown > DRAW_LEAD or _playback.get_current_node() != &"idle":
		return
	var target := nearest_target()
	if target:
		locked_target = target
		_locked_pos = target.global_position
		shot_armed = true
		_playback.travel(&"shoot")


## Ends a shot that has not released: clears the guard and the target, returns the tree to idle at
## once. Never writes release_window (§5.4); a stale true is ignored because shot_armed is false.
func cancel_shot() -> void:
	shot_armed = false
	locked_target = null
	_playback.start(&"idle")


func nearest_target() -> Scarecrow:
	var best: Scarecrow = null
	var best_dist := INF
	var half_cone := deg_to_rad(Tuning.FIRE_CONE_DEG / 2.0)
	for enemy in get_tree().get_nodes_in_group("enemies"):
		var s := enemy as Scarecrow
		if s == null or s.is_dead():
			continue
		var to := s.global_position - global_position
		if absf(Vector2.UP.angle_to(to)) > half_cone:
			continue
		if to.length() < best_dist:
			best_dist = to.length()
			best = s
	return best


## The locked target is alive and still inside the cone (same test as nearest_target()).
func _target_held() -> bool:
	if not is_instance_valid(locked_target) or locked_target.is_queued_for_deletion() or locked_target.is_dead():
		return false
	var to := locked_target.global_position - global_position
	return absf(Vector2.UP.angle_to(to)) <= deg_to_rad(Tuning.FIRE_CONE_DEG / 2.0)


func _fire_at(target_pos: Vector2) -> void:
	var arrow := ARROW_SCENE.instantiate() as Arrow
	var from := global_position + Vector2(0, -24)
	arrow.launch(from, target_pos - from)
	(arrows_parent if arrows_parent else get_parent()).add_child(arrow)
	fired.emit(arrow)

class_name Game
extends Node2D
## One prototype run: survive SURVIVE_TIME seconds of scarecrows without losing the gate.
## Owns the run state (gate HP, elapsed time, kills, win/lose). Restart with R/Enter at the end.

signal state_changed(new_state: State)

enum State { PLAYING, WON, LOST }

const SCARECROW_SCENE := preload("res://game/scarecrow.tscn")
const ARCHER_START := Vector2(640, 572)

@export var spawning_enabled := true
## (start, end) spawn interval used instead of Tuning's when non-zero; only tools/balance_sim.gd sets it.
var spawn_interval_override := Vector2.ZERO

var state: State = State.PLAYING
var gate_hp: float = Tuning.GATE_HP
var elapsed := 0.0
var kills := 0
var spawn_timer := 0.0
var rng := RandomNumberGenerator.new()

@onready var world: Node2D = $World
@onready var enemies: Node2D = $World/Enemies
@onready var arrows: Node2D = $World/Arrows
@onready var archer: Archer = $World/Archer


func _ready() -> void:
	rng.randomize()
	archer.arrows_parent = arrows
	reset()


func reset() -> void:
	for child in enemies.get_children() + arrows.get_children():
		if child.is_in_group("enemies"):
			child.remove_from_group("enemies")
		child.queue_free()
	gate_hp = Tuning.GATE_HP
	elapsed = 0.0
	kills = 0
	spawn_timer = 1.0
	archer.position = ARCHER_START
	archer.fire_cooldown = 0.0
	archer.cancel_shot()
	world.process_mode = Node.PROCESS_MODE_INHERIT
	_set_state(State.PLAYING)


func spawn_scarecrow(at: Vector2) -> Scarecrow:
	var s := SCARECROW_SCENE.instantiate() as Scarecrow
	s.position = at
	s.died.connect(func() -> void: kills += 1)
	s.attacking_gate.connect(_on_attacking_gate)
	enemies.add_child(s)
	return s


func spawn_interval() -> float:
	var t := clampf(elapsed / Tuning.SURVIVE_TIME, 0.0, 1.0)
	if spawn_interval_override != Vector2.ZERO:
		return lerpf(spawn_interval_override.x, spawn_interval_override.y, t)
	return lerpf(Tuning.SPAWN_INTERVAL_START, Tuning.SPAWN_INTERVAL_END, t)


func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void:
	if state != State.PLAYING:
		return
	elapsed += delta
	if elapsed >= Tuning.SURVIVE_TIME:
		_end(State.WON)
		return
	if spawning_enabled:
		spawn_timer -= delta
		if spawn_timer <= 0.0:
			spawn_timer += spawn_interval()
			spawn_scarecrow(Vector2(rng.randf_range(60.0, Tuning.VIEW.x - 60.0), -40.0))


func _unhandled_input(event: InputEvent) -> void:
	if state != State.PLAYING and event.is_action_pressed("restart"):
		reset()


func _on_attacking_gate(amount: float) -> void:
	if state != State.PLAYING:
		return
	gate_hp = maxf(gate_hp - amount, 0.0)
	if gate_hp <= 0.0:
		_end(State.LOST)


func _end(result: State) -> void:
	world.process_mode = Node.PROCESS_MODE_DISABLED   # freeze the field; HUD shows the result
	_set_state(result)


func _set_state(s: State) -> void:
	state = s
	state_changed.emit(s)

## Meadow, castle wall and gate, drawn in code (flat cartoon colours).

const MEADOW := Color("6da34d")
const TUFT := Color("5a8f3e")
const STONE := Color("8d8f94")
const MORTAR := Color("6f7176")
const WALKWAY := Color("a3a5aa")
const GATE := Color("3b2f2a")


func _draw() -> void:
	var w := Tuning.VIEW.x
	var top := Tuning.WALL_TOP
	draw_rect(Rect2(0, 0, w, Tuning.VIEW.y), MEADOW)
	var rng := RandomNumberGenerator.new()
	rng.seed = 7                                   # same tufts every run
	for i in 70:
		var p := Vector2(rng.randf_range(0, w), rng.randf_range(0, top - 40))
		draw_line(p, p + Vector2(-3, -7), TUFT, 2.0)
		draw_line(p, p + Vector2(3, -8), TUFT, 2.0)
	draw_rect(Rect2(0, top, w, Tuning.VIEW.y - top), STONE)
	draw_rect(Rect2(0, top - 4, w, 10), WALKWAY)
	for row in 4:                                  # brick courses
		var y := top + 6 + row * 28.0
		draw_line(Vector2(0, y), Vector2(w, y), MORTAR, 2.0)
		var offset := 0.0 if row % 2 == 0 else 32.0
		var x := offset
		while x < w:
			draw_line(Vector2(x, y), Vector2(x, y + 28), MORTAR, 2.0)
			x += 64.0
	draw_rect(Rect2(596, top + 34, 88, Tuning.VIEW.y - top - 34), GATE)
	draw_circle(Vector2(640, top + 34), 44, GATE)
class_name Scarecrow
extends Node2D
## Straw Scarecrow: walks down to the wall and hits the gate. Straw burns.
## Owns the Burning state: burn_time_left > 0 means burning. Fire refreshes it to the full
## BURN_DURATION (a second hit does not stack damage). Timed in physics time, so it follows
## Engine.time_scale and stops while the tree is paused.

signal burning_started
signal burning_ended
signal died
signal attacking_gate(amount: float)
signal hit_taken(position: Vector2)

const BURN_END_EPSILON := 1e-9      # s; float residue below this counts as burnt out

var hp: float = Tuning.SCARECROW_HP
var burn_time_left: float = 0.0
var at_wall := false


func _ready() -> void:
	add_to_group("enemies")
	at_wall = position.y >= Tuning.SCARECROW_STOP_Y


func is_burning() -> bool:
	return burn_time_left > 0.0


func is_dead() -> bool:
	return hp <= 0.0


func hit(damage: float, element: StringName) -> void:
	if is_dead():
		return
	hp -= damage
	if element == &"fire":
		ignite()
	hit_taken.emit(global_position)
	_check_death()


func ignite() -> void:
	var was_burning := is_burning()
	burn_time_left = Tuning.BURN_DURATION
	if not was_burning:
		burning_started.emit()


func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void:
	if is_dead() or is_queued_for_deletion():   # a reset in the same tick must not hit the gate
		return
	if is_burning():
		var burned := minf(delta, burn_time_left)
		hp -= Tuning.BURN_DPS * burned
		burn_time_left -= delta
		# Summing 240 deltas of 1/60 leaves ~1e-14 instead of 0, which used to add a 241st tick.
		if burn_time_left <= BURN_END_EPSILON:
			burn_time_left = 0.0
			burning_ended.emit()
		_check_death()
		if is_dead():
			return
	if at_wall:
		attacking_gate.emit(Tuning.SCARECROW_GATE_DPS * delta)
	else:
		position.y = minf(position.y + Tuning.SCARECROW_SPEED * delta, Tuning.SCARECROW_STOP_Y)
		at_wall = position.y >= Tuning.SCARECROW_STOP_Y


func _check_death() -> void:
	if is_dead():
		remove_from_group("enemies")
		died.emit()
		queue_free()
class_name Tuning
## Every gameplay number in one place.
## "GDD" = Mimic Keep GDD v0.1 (Assignment 4); "proto" = chosen for this prototype, to be playtested.

const VIEW := Vector2(1280, 720)
const WALL_TOP := 600.0                # y of the wall walk the archer stands on

const ARCHER_SPEED := 420.0            # px/s, GDD 5.1
const ARCHER_MARGIN := 40.0            # px kept between the archer and the screen edge
const FIRE_INTERVAL := 0.6             # s between auto-fired arrows, proto
const FIRE_CONE_DEG := 120.0           # main weapon targets inside this upward cone, GDD 6.2

const ARROW_SPEED := 900.0             # px/s, proto
const ARROW_DAMAGE := 10.0             # proto
const ARROW_HIT_RADIUS := 26.0         # px from the scarecrow's centre, proto

const SCARECROW_HP := 40.0             # proto
const SCARECROW_SPEED := 45.0          # px/s down the screen, proto
const SCARECROW_GATE_DPS := 5.0        # gate damage per scarecrow at the wall, proto
# Was WALL_TOP - 30 (570): level with the archer (y 572), so a scarecrow at the wall sat ~90 deg off
# the fire cone and was only targeted within 3 px (Rui's playtest 2026-10-29). 500 fixed the aim but
# looked too far from the wall; Rui chose 530 from 500/520/530/540: feet 30 px above the walkway, in
# the cone within +-73 px of the archer.
const SCARECROW_STOP_Y := WALL_TOP - 70.0

const BURN_DURATION := 4.0             # s, GDD 6.3 "Burning: 4 dmg/s for 4 s"

## The hero on the wall walk: slides along X only and fires on its own (GDD 5.1, 6.2).
## Aims at the nearest scarecrow inside the upward cone; holds fire when there is none.
## Owns the shot state machine (CHANGE-BRIEF §5, §6): it decides when to draw (travel("shoot")) and
## when to cancel (playback.start("idle")); the AnimationTree only plays the clips and keys
## release_window, which this script reads and never writes.

signal fired(arrow: Arrow)

const ARROW_SCENE := preload("res://game/arrow.tscn")
## s; the draw starts when fire_cooldown is at most this (brief §5.2: 18 ticks from travel("shoot")
## to the first true read of release_window, so back-to-back shots keep the 36-tick cadence).
## Here, not in tuning.gd, because tuning.gd is out of scope for this change.
const DRAW_LEAD := 0.3

var arrows_parent: Node
var fire_cooldown := 0.0
var release_window := false          # written only by Archer/AnimationTree (idle and shoot clips)
var shot_armed := false              # true from travel("shoot") until the arrow, a cancel or a restart
var locked_target: Scarecrow = null  # taken when the draw starts (brief §5.3)
var _locked_pos := Vector2.ZERO      # locked target's global position, recorded every armed tick

@onready var _playback: AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback = $AnimationTree.get("parameters/playback")


func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void:
	var axis := Input.get_axis("move_left", "move_right")
	position.x = clampf(position.x + axis * Tuning.ARCHER_SPEED * delta,
			Tuning.ARCHER_MARGIN, Tuning.VIEW.x - Tuning.ARCHER_MARGIN)
	fire_cooldown = maxf(fire_cooldown - delta, 0.0)
	if shot_armed:
		if release_window:
			# Active frame: the arrow goes even if the target was lost on this same tick (§5.5).
			var aim := locked_target.global_position if is_instance_valid(locked_target) else _locked_pos
			_fire_at(aim)
			fire_cooldown = Tuning.FIRE_INTERVAL
			shot_armed = false
			locked_target = null
		elif not _target_held():
			cancel_shot()   # startup: target died or left the cone; no new draw on this tick
		else:
			_locked_pos = locked_target.global_position
		return
	if fire_cooldown > DRAW_LEAD or _playback.get_current_node() != &"idle":
		return
	var target := nearest_target()
	if target:
		locked_target = target
		_locked_pos = target.global_position
		shot_armed = true
		_playback.travel(&"shoot")


## Ends a shot that has not released: clears the guard and the target, returns the tree to idle at
## once. Never writes release_window (§5.4); a stale true is ignored because shot_armed is false.
func cancel_shot() -> void:
	shot_armed = false
	locked_target = null
	_playback.start(&"idle")


func nearest_target() -> Scarecrow:
	var best: Scarecrow = null
	var best_dist := INF
	var half_cone := deg_to_rad(Tuning.FIRE_CONE_DEG / 2.0)
	for enemy in get_tree().get_nodes_in_group("enemies"):
		var s := enemy as Scarecrow
		if s == null or s.is_dead():
			continue
		var to := s.global_position - global_position
		if absf(Vector2.UP.angle_to(to)) > half_cone:
			continue
		if to.length() < best_dist:
			best_dist = to.length()
			best = s
	return best


## The locked target is alive and still inside the cone (same test as nearest_target()).
func _target_held() -> bool:
	if not is_instance_valid(locked_target) or locked_target.is_queued_for_deletion() or locked_target.is_dead():
		return false
	var to := locked_target.global_position - global_position
	return absf(Vector2.UP.angle_to(to)) <= deg_to_rad(Tuning.FIRE_CONE_DEG / 2.0)


func _fire_at(target_pos: Vector2) -> void:
	var arrow := ARROW_SCENE.instantiate() as Arrow
	var from := global_position + Vector2(0, -24)
	arrow.launch(from, target_pos - from)
	(arrows_parent if arrows_parent else get_parent()).add_child(arrow)
	fired.emit(arrow)

extends Node2D
## One prototype run: survive SURVIVE_TIME seconds of scarecrows without losing the gate.
## Owns the run state (gate HP, elapsed time, kills, win/lose). Restart with R/Enter at the end.

signal state_changed(new_state: State)

enum State { PLAYING, WON, LOST }

const SCARECROW_SCENE := preload("res://game/scarecrow.tscn")
const ARCHER_START := Vector2(640, 572)

@export var spawning_enabled := true
## (start, end) spawn interval used instead of Tuning's when non-zero; only tools/balance_sim.gd sets it.
var spawn_interval_override := Vector2.ZERO

var state: State = State.PLAYING
var gate_hp: float = Tuning.GATE_HP
var elapsed := 0.0
var kills := 0
var spawn_timer := 0.0
var rng := RandomNumberGenerator.new()

@onready var world: Node2D = $World
@onready var enemies: Node2D = $World/Enemies
@onready var arrows: Node2D = $World/Arrows
@onready var archer: Archer = $World/Archer


func _ready() -> void:
	rng.randomize()
	archer.arrows_parent = arrows
	reset()


func reset() -> void:
	for child in enemies.get_children() + arrows.get_children():
		if child.is_in_group("enemies"):
			child.remove_from_group("enemies")
		child.queue_free()
	gate_hp = Tuning.GATE_HP
	elapsed = 0.0
	kills = 0
	spawn_timer = 1.0
	archer.position = ARCHER_START
	archer.fire_cooldown = 0.0
	archer.cancel_shot()
	world.process_mode = Node.PROCESS_MODE_INHERIT
	_set_state(State.PLAYING)


func spawn_scarecrow(at: Vector2) -> Scarecrow:
	var s := SCARECROW_SCENE.instantiate() as Scarecrow
	s.position = at
	s.died.connect(func() -> void: kills += 1)
	s.attacking_gate.connect(_on_attacking_gate)
	enemies.add_child(s)
	return s


func spawn_interval() -> float:
	var t := clampf(elapsed / Tuning.SURVIVE_TIME, 0.0, 1.0)
	if spawn_interval_override != Vector2.ZERO:
		return lerpf(spawn_interval_override.x, spawn_interval_override.y, t)
	return lerpf(Tuning.SPAWN_INTERVAL_START, Tuning.SPAWN_INTERVAL_END, t)


func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void:
	if state != State.PLAYING:
		return
	elapsed += delta
	if elapsed >= Tuning.SURVIVE_TIME:
		_end(State.WON)
		return
	if spawning_enabled:
		spawn_timer -= delta
		if spawn_timer <= 0.0:
			spawn_timer += spawn_interval()
			spawn_scarecrow(Vector2(rng.randf_range(60.0, Tuning.VIEW.x - 60.0), -40.0))


func _unhandled_input(event: InputEvent) -> void:
	if state != State.PLAYING and event.is_action_pressed("restart"):
		reset()


func _on_attacking_gate(amount: float) -> void:
	if state != State.PLAYING:
		return
	gate_hp = maxf(gate_hp - amount, 0.0)
	if gate_hp <= 0.0:
		_end(State.LOST)


func _end(result: State) -> void:
	world.process_mode = Node.PROCESS_MODE_DISABLED   # freeze the field; HUD shows the result
	_set_state(result)


func _set_state(s: State) -> void:
	state = s
	state_changed.emit(s)

class_name Scarecrow
extends Node2D
## Straw Scarecrow: walks down to the wall and hits the gate. Straw burns.
## Owns the Burning state: burn_time_left > 0 means burning. Fire refreshes it to the full
## BURN_DURATION (a second hit does not stack damage). Timed in physics time, so it follows
## Engine.time_scale and stops while the tree is paused.

signal burning_started
signal burning_ended
signal died
signal attacking_gate(amount: float)
signal hit_taken(position: Vector2)

const BURN_END_EPSILON := 1e-9      # s; float residue below this counts as burnt out

var hp: float = Tuning.SCARECROW_HP
var burn_time_left: float = 0.0
var at_wall := false


func _ready() -> void:
	add_to_group("enemies")
	at_wall = position.y >= Tuning.SCARECROW_STOP_Y


func is_burning() -> bool:
	return burn_time_left > 0.0


func is_dead() -> bool:
	return hp <= 0.0


func hit(damage: float, element: StringName) -> void:
	if is_dead():
		return
	hp -= damage
	if element == &"fire":
		ignite()
	hit_taken.emit(global_position)
	_check_death()


func ignite() -> void:
	var was_burning := is_burning()
	burn_time_left = Tuning.BURN_DURATION
	if not was_burning:
		burning_started.emit()


func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void:
	if is_dead() or is_queued_for_deletion():   # a reset in the same tick must not hit the gate
		return
	if is_burning():
		var burned := minf(delta, burn_time_left)
		hp -= Tuning.BURN_DPS * burned
		burn_time_left -= delta
		# Summing 240 deltas of 1/60 leaves ~1e-14 instead of 0, which used to add a 241st tick.
		if burn_time_left <= BURN_END_EPSILON:
			burn_time_left = 0.0
			burning_ended.emit()
		_check_death()
		if is_dead():
			return
	if at_wall:

var _seen_fire := false

@onready var _enemies: Node2D = $World/Enemies

@onready var _pivot: Node2D = $World/Archer/Rig/BowPivot

I've written `godot/previews/shoot_preview.tscn` and `godot/previews/shoot_preview.gd`. Driven only by `archer.gd`'s own rule, the draw starts on frame 10, the arrow appears on frame 19 and the archer is back in idle on frame 25. Both test suites still pass (107/0 and 38/0). Two things differ from what you asked for: an extra frame-number column, and when the target is removed (both below).

**What the preview does.** It shows the real background, and the real `archer.tscn` at (640, 572) with `arrows_parent` set to its own `World/Arrows`. The preview only places and removes its own scarecrow, connects to `fired`, and reads values. It never calls `travel()`, `start()` or `cancel_shot()` and never writes archer, tree or clip state.

**Trigger.** One scarecrow is placed at (640, 420) on physics tick 20. The preview's root runs before the archer within a tick, so `archer.gd` calls `travel("shoot")` on that same tick. I picked tick 20 rather than 21, the other tick of frame 10, because then every rendered frame falls exactly on a 1/30 s key of the clip, so strip frame 10+k shows clip frame k.

Measured landings with `--fixed-fps 30`:

| Event | Frame (tick) |
|---|---|
| Draw starts (shot_armed true, clip frame 0) | **10** (tick 20) |
| `release_window` true, full draw pose (clip frame 8) | **18** (tick 37) |
| Arrow spawns, `fired` (pose already clip frame 9, `release_window` false) | **19** (tick 38) |
| Back in idle (clip end, frame 15) | **25** (tick 51) |
| Repeat: target placed again, draw starts | tick 112, frame **56** |

**Decision for you: the arrow shows one strip frame late.** The tree writes `release_window` true on tick 37, but `archer.gd` reads it on tick 38, which is in frame 19. So in the strip, frame 18 shows the full draw with no arrow, and frame 19 shows the first recovery pose with the arrow just leaving. §11's row for clip frame 8 says the arrow should leave on that frame. This is the 1-tick read delay that brief §5.2 already accounts for, and fixing it would mean changing game files, which this step doesn't allow. Triggering on tick 21 instead puts the arrow on frame 19 together with an in-between pose that isn't on a key. So the §11 row's wording needs your call.

**Deviations from your spec:**
1. **Frame number.** Headless, `Engine.get_frames_drawn()` stays at **0** because nothing is drawn. I kept it as the first field and added `pframe`, a count of `_process` calls from 0, as the second. Frame n holds ticks 2n and 2n+1. I couldn't check headless that `get_frames_drawn()` equals `pframe` in a windowed Movie Maker run.
2. **Target removed before the 1 s wait, not after.** If the target stays in the cone, `archer.gd` starts the next draw 18 ticks after the release (§5.2), so you'd get back-to-back shots instead of one. The preview therefore removes the target as soon as the tree is idle and no arrow is left (tick 52). It then waits 60 ticks with nothing on the field and places a new one on a tick of the same parity as tick 20, so each repeat lines up with frames the same way.

I've written `godot/previews/shoot_preview.tscn` and `godot/previews/shoot_preview.gd`. Driven only by `archer.gd`'s own rule, the draw starts on frame 10, the arrow appears on frame 19 and the archer is back in idle on frame 25. Both test suites still pass (107/0 and 38/0). Two things differ from what you asked for: an extra frame-number column, and when the target is removed (both below).

**What the preview does.** It shows the real background, and the real `archer.tscn` at (640, 572) with `arrows_parent` set to its own `World/Arrows`. The preview only places and removes its own scarecrow, connects to `fired`, and reads values. It never calls `travel()`, `start()` or `cancel_shot()` and never writes archer, tree or clip state.

**Trigger.** One scarecrow is placed at (640, 420) on physics tick 20. The preview's root runs before the archer within a tick, so `archer.gd` calls `travel("shoot")` on that same tick. I picked tick 20 rather than 21, the other tick of frame 10, because then every rendered frame falls exactly on a 1/30 s key of the clip, so strip frame 10+k shows clip frame k.

Measured landings with `--fixed-fps 30`:

| Event | Frame (tick) |
|---|---|
| Draw starts (shot_armed true, clip frame 0) | **10** (tick 20) |
| `release_window` true, full draw pose (clip frame 8) | **18** (tick 37) |
| Arrow spawns, `fired` (pose already clip frame 9, `release_window` false) | **19** (tick 38) |
| Back in idle (clip end, frame 15) | **25** (tick 51) |
| Repeat: target placed again, draw starts | tick 112, frame **56** |

**Decision for you: the arrow shows one strip frame late.** The tree writes `release_window` true on tick 37, but `archer.gd` reads it on tick 38, which is in frame 19. So in the strip, frame 18 shows the full draw with no arrow, and frame 19 shows the first recovery pose with the arrow just leaving. §11's row for clip frame 8 says the arrow should leave on that frame. This is the 1-tick read delay that brief §5.2 already accounts for, and fixing it would mean changing game files, which this step doesn't allow. Triggering on tick 21 instead puts the arrow on frame 19 together with an in-between pose that isn't on a key. So the §11 row's wording needs your call.

**Deviations from your spec:**
1. **Frame number.** Headless, `Engine.get_frames_drawn()` stays at **0** because nothing is drawn. I kept it as the first field and added `pframe`, a count of `_process` calls from 0, as the second. Frame n holds ticks 2n and 2n+1. I couldn't check headless that `get_frames_drawn()` equals `pframe` in a windowed Movie Maker run.
2. **Target removed before the 1 s wait, not after.** If the target stays in the cone, `archer.gd` starts the next draw 18 ticks after the release (§5.2), so you'd get back-to-back shots instead of one. The preview therefore removes the target as soon as the tree is idle and no arrow is left (tick 52). It then waits 60 ticks with nothing on the field and places a new one on a tick of the same parity as tick 20, so each repeat lines up with frames the same way.
